Consult Summary:
- Telehealth consult for adult male with ~2 months of fatigue, low mood, insomnia, reduced appetite, decreased libido, and exertional shortness of breath; history of hypothyroidism on thyroxine.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Difficulty waking, very low energy, reduced appetite, trouble sleeping, decreased concentration and focus.
- Associated symptoms: Low mood; decreased libido and disinterest in sex over past few months; exertional shortness of breath when playing sports; denies suicidal ideation or thoughts of harm to others; no change in vision.
- Pertinent negatives: Denies SI/HI; no visual changes; not waking early (reports difficulty sleeping instead).
- Past medical history: Hypothyroidism.
- Medications: Thyroxine (dose/route/frequency not documented); currently taking.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Family history: Father died by suicide ~15 years ago; otherwise denies family psychiatric or major medical conditions; mother well; only child.
- Social history: Married; started a new job ~2 months ago; onset may coincide with job change.
- Preventive care: Not discussed.

Examination:
- Vitals:
- Findings:

Impression:
- Fatigue with low mood, insomnia, decreased appetite, and reduced libido; exertional dyspnea. History of hypothyroidism on treatment. No current suicidal ideation. Further evaluation required.

Plan:
- Arrange in-person GP appointment in the next few days for physical examination.
- Order blood tests and further investigations (specific tests not detailed in transcript).
- Continue with plan to evaluate causes of tiredness and associated symptoms; follow up after in-person assessment.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: Full review of systems; vitals; physical exam; medication dose/route/frequency and adherence details; thyroid function results; depression/anxiety screening; substance use history; weight change; sleep pattern details; safety planning and crisis resources; occupational stress assessment.
● Internal conflicts: Morning erections—patient first agreed he had not noticed them recently, then later stated there has not been a change (conflict noted). Thyroid history briefly confused as “hyper” by clinician, corrected by patient to hypothyroidism.
● Transcript quality: Minor audio/freeze issues and interruptions; otherwise understandable.
